fields.body: Power With is for leaders who have built a great deal and still sense that something essential remains out of reach. It shows you how to hold your influence so the people closest to you grow stronger in your presence.

fields.headline: The drive that builds companies can dismantle marriages.

paragraphs.text: Most people treat their success and their relational struggles as separate problems. The career is going well. The marriage is hard. Both run on the same operating system.

The strategies that win in competition are specific. Control, self-sufficiency, the refusal to be affected, the need to stay ahead. At home and on a team, those same strategies create distance. The cost builds so slowly that most people see it only once it runs deep.

fields.subhead: The control that commands respect can silence the people who love you most. The armor that makes you formidable can make you unreachable.

cards.body: Every conversation shapes one. Every meeting, every dinner and every decision shapes the trust and safety of the people around you. You hold more power than you may realize.
cards.definition: Power is the capacity to shape outcomes.
cards.label: Power

cards.body: It can look like competence, decisiveness and strength. In a crisis it has its place. As a default it produces distance, distrust and isolation, slowly, beneath a life that still looks highly functional.
cards.definition: Power over is the use of influence to control.
cards.label: Power over

cards.body: It holds authority and relationship at the same time. You lead, decide and act while staying connected to the people your choices affect. It is the more disciplined orientation, and it asks more of you than power over ever did.
cards.definition: Power with is the use of influence to stay in relationship.
cards.label: Power with

fields.closing: The trust you build carries forward in your absence. That is lasting influence.
fields.headline: A language for power.
fields.intro: Three terms carry the whole book. They are simple to define. Once you hold them, you see every relationship, every team and every room differently.

fields.description: The strategies that build success often erode the relationships success depends on. Four parts and ten principles show you how to hold your influence and stay connected to the people who matter most.

fields.lede: Sophia Life writes from the field. For more than a decade she has studied the patterns in this book up close and practiced the principles that change them.
fields.name: Sophia Life
fields.names: Carol Gilligan · Martin Buber · Jessica Benjamin · Terry Real · Otto Kernberg · Heinz Kohut · Donald Winnicott · Joseph Burgo · Daniel Schmachtenberger

paragraphs.text: She paired that practice with years of study across depth psychology, attachment theory, developmental psychology, neuroscience, systems thinking, leadership theory and relational philosophy. The result is a synthesis written for the person living inside these patterns, and for the person who loves them.

Sophia is a coach and organizational consultant with a background in urban planning and product development. She writes The Quality of Life on Substack and lives in Boulder, Colorado. [Years in practice, notable clients and speaking credits.]
